question:
A function comparison activity considers $p(x)=\csc^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)$. The reciprocal inside the inverse cosecant requires $x\neq0$, while the inverse-cosecant argument must satisfy an absolute-value restriction. Students are asked to compare $p$ with $y=\sin^{-1}x$ by using $\csc^{-1}t=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{t}\right)$ whenever $|t|\geq1$. They must determine how excluding $x=0$ changes the domain, range, and graph even though the two expressions give the same value at every permitted input. Values at $x=1$, $x=-1$, $x=\dfrac{1}{2}$, and $x=-\dfrac{1}{2}$ are used as reference points.

(a) Determine the domain of $p$.

(b) Establish the simplified form of $p(x)$ on its domain.

(c) Determine the exact range of $p$.

(d) Find the four reference points and explain how the graph differs from $y=\sin^{-1}x$.
explanation:
(a)
For $\csc^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)$ to be defined,
$$\left|\frac{1}{x}\right|\geq1$$
with $x\neq0$. Therefore,
$$0<|x|\leq1$$
Hence, the domain is
$$[-1,0)\cup(0,1]$$

(b)
Using the reciprocal relation,
$$\csc^{-1}t=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{t}\right)$$
with $t=\dfrac{1}{x}$ gives
$$p(x)=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{\frac{1}{x}}\right)=\sin^{-1}x$$
This equality holds for every $x\in[-1,0)\cup(0,1]$.

(c)
The range of $\sin^{-1}x$ on $[-1,1]$ is $\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$. However, $x=0$ is excluded from the domain, so the value $\sin^{-1}(0)=0$ is not attained. Therefore,
$$\text{Range}=\left[-\frac{\pi}{2},0\right)\cup\left(0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right]$$

(d)
The required values are
$$p(1)=\frac{\pi}{2},\qquad p(-1)=-\frac{\pi}{2}$$
and
$$p\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=\frac{\pi}{6},\qquad p\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)=-\frac{\pi}{6}$$
Thus, the reference points are $\left(1,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, $\left(-1,-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, $\left(\dfrac{1}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$, and $\left(-\dfrac{1}{2},-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$. The graph coincides with $y=\sin^{-1}x$ except that the point $(0,0)$ is removed.

options.A:
(a) Domain: $[-1,1]$

(b) $p(x)=\sin^{-1}x$

(c) Range: $\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$

(d) Reference points: $\left(\pm1,\pm\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ and $\left(\pm\dfrac{1}{2},\pm\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$; the graph is identical to $y=\sin^{-1}x$ with no point removed
options.B:
(a) Domain: $(-\infty,-1]\cup[1,\infty)$

(b) $p(x)=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)$

(c) Range: $\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2},0\right)\cup\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$

(d) Reference points: $\left(1,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ and $\left(-1,-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ only; the graph has two unbounded branches
options.C:
(a) Domain: $[-1,0)\cup(0,1]$

(b) $p(x)=\sin^{-1}x$ on its domain

(c) Range: $\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2},0\right)\cup\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$

(d) Reference points: $\left(1,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, $\left(-1,-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, $\left(\dfrac{1}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$, and $\left(-\dfrac{1}{2},-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$; the graph is $y=\sin^{-1}x$ with $(0,0)$ removed
options.D:
(a) Domain: $(-1,0)\cup(0,1)$

(b) $p(x)=\cos^{-1}x$ on its domain

(c) Range: $(0,\pi)$

(d) Reference points: $\left(\dfrac{1}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$ and $\left(-\dfrac{1}{2},\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)$; the graph is $y=\cos^{-1}x$ with its endpoints removed
